advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the top-level shared `deploy-backoff` gate (line 499) should still block the independent mcp path, or gate only the bot path (mirroring the new mcp-scoped backoff).
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:500 `log "backoff active for $TARGET ..."; exit 0` — exits the whole script before the mcp block at 682
Comment at infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:59-63 states the two paths' failure state 'is independent too', but the shared BACKOFF_FILE gate still blocks mcp when only the bot failed.
advisory.finding: The top-level shared backoff gate still exits the ENTIRE script when `deploy-backoff` (the review-bot's shared backoff) is active, so a review-bot deploy failure suppresses the now-independent mcp blue-green path on every subsequent tick until the bot backoff window elapses. The change made mcp's failure state independent of the bot (MCP_BACKOFF_FILE) but left the reverse direction coupled through this global gate.
scenarios: Shared src/rebar change; bot build fails and records deploy-backoff; the mcp fix that would repair the box cannot deploy while the bot backoff window is open.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that seeds a future-epoch `mcp-deploy-backoff` for $TARGET and asserts the mcp deploy is skipped (logs 'mcp backoff active', no `run --name rebar-mcp-*`) while the window is open.
evidence: search of tests for `mcp_backoff_active` returned `(no matches)`
search of tests for `mcp-deploy-backoff` returns only the unlink at line 511 — no test writes a future-epoch mcp-deploy-backoff and asserts the next tick skips the deploy

Named violating input: a state file `mcp-deploy-backoff` = `<TARGET> 3 <now+3600>` on a tick with a live mcp delta — the new gate must log `mcp backoff active` and NOT run `run --name rebar-mcp-*`; nothing asserts this.
autodeploy.sh (added): `mcp_deployed="$(cat "$MCP_SHA_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"` then the validation falling back to $DEPLOYED
search of tests for `mcp-deployed-sha` returns only a docstring mention at line 1191 — no test writes the file

Named violating input: `mcp-deployed-sha` file containing `garbage` (or `zzz...`) — the new guard must fall back to $DEPLOYED and deploy exactly as a first-run box; nothing exercises the invalid-marker branch.
advisory.finding: The newly-added mcp_backoff_active gate — which SKIPS the mcp blue-green deploy while the mcp-scoped backoff window is in effect (autodeploy.sh:679-682) — has no test. test_mcp_failure_on_a_deferred_tick_does_not_backoff_the_bot writes the backoff (via record_mcp_backoff_failure) but never runs a subsequent tick to verify the mcp deploy is throttled while the window is open; the only other reference to the file is an unlink at line 511 that models elapsed time.
merged_from: The newly-added mcp-deployed-sha marker validation — an empty or non-rev-parseable marker falls back to $DEPLOYED rather than poisoning the diff range (autodeploy.sh new block: `if [ -z "$mcp_deployed" ] || ! git ... rev-parse --verify ...; then mcp_deployed="$DEPLOYED"; fi`) — has no test. No test seeds a garbage mcp-deployed-sha and verifies the tick still decides the mcp delta from $DEPLOYED.
scenarios: An mcp failure sets the backoff; a subsequent tick within the window must not rebuild+cutover mcp

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert that an mcp deploy failure emits a `deploy_failed` metric carrying `component=mcp` (extend test_mcp_failure_on_a_deferred_tick_does_not_backoff_the_bot).
evidence: autodeploy.sh record_mcp_backoff_failure (added): `err deploy_failed "component=mcp target=$TARGET fail#$n backoff=${wait}s"`
search of tests for `deploy_failed` returned `(no matches)`
search of tests for `component=mcp` returned `(no matches)`

test_mcp_failure_on_a_deferred_tick_does_not_backoff_the_bot asserts only `"mcp-unhealthy" in result.stdout + result.stderr` and the ABSENCE of a shared deploy-backoff — never the deploy_failed/component=mcp emission the contract promises.
advisory.finding: The stated metric-continuity contract — 'The metric stays deploy_failed so existing alarming still fires, with a component= marker to say which path failed' — is untested. record_mcp_backoff_failure emits `err deploy_failed "component=mcp ..."`, but no test asserts `deploy_failed` or `component=mcp` is emitted on an mcp failure; the failure test asserts only `mcp-unhealthy`.
scenarios: An mcp deploy failure must still fire the existing deploy_failed alarm, tagged component=mcp

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Prevent an mcp deploy failure from forcing the review-bot to redeploy every tick (track bot completion independently, or do not let mcp's `exit 1` strand a successful bot deploy without advancing its recorded sha).
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:688 `err mcp-checkout-failed ...; record_mcp_backoff_failure; exit 1` (and the sibling exit-1 paths at 691,707,710,713,721,730,738,751,760) run after the bot block at 666-668 already completed
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:836 `echo "$TARGET" > "$SHA_FILE.tmp" && mv ...` — only advanced at the footer, unreachable once the mcp block exit 1s
The PR only added MCP_SHA_FILE for the mcp path; there is no bot-deployed-sha, so a successful bot deploy in a tick that then fails mcp is not recorded and repeats next tick.
blocking.finding: An mcp deploy failure aborts the whole script (`record_mcp_backoff_failure; exit 1`) AFTER the review-bot has already successfully redeployed in the same tick, but `SHA_FILE`/`deployed-sha` only advances at the footer (line 836) which is never reached. On a shared `src/rebar` change (both triggers match), the next tick still sees `changed "$BOT_PATHS"` true and rebuilds+restarts the review-bot again — every tick until mcp succeeds. This is the mirror of the very coupling the PR set out to remove: mcp failure now forces redundant bot redeploys (and eventual in-flight-review kills once the drain bound is exhausted). The bot path has no per-component completion marker equivalent to the new MCP_SHA_FILE.
scenarios: A shared src/rebar commit lands; mcp is chronically unhealthy (fails /health) but the bot builds fine — the bot is rebuilt + `docker compose up -d`'d on every ~2-minute tick until mcp recovers.
